archetypes.gap: The homepage currently imports as a standard page; the schema does not reserve one homepage archetype or enforce ownership of the root route.
The discriminator is descriptive only; block allowlists and minimum content are not schema-enforced.
The product archetype has no enforced product-specific content invariant.
The landing archetype is available to editors but has no enforced layout contract.
Legal and policy templates are not represented by a dedicated schema invariant, and cookie-category shortcode semantics are not implemented.
The first-party form block, submission storage/delivery, validation, consent, spam protection, and conversion-page invariant are not implemented.
The market-matrix archetype and component are not present, and all referenced hub and venue destinations must become managed public route owners.
articleListing is neither required for index pages nor restricted from other page archetypes.
A full article can be published without a body because layout is not conditionally required.

Imported listing-only records currently receive published internal paths and are linked from Insights, producing empty detail pages. Production must either import a full body, use an explicit external destination, create a redirect, or keep the record non-routable.
The 15 listing-linked learning videos have no Payload collection or frontend route owner.
Public-page hubs do not conditionally require a path; their layout may rely on the renderer fallback rather than an explicit archetype contract.
The importer omits paths, but the schema does not prevent an editor from assigning a public path or layout to a map-only hub.
The target contentMode discriminator does not exist yet, so dependency-only venue records cannot be distinguished from the 66 public venue details.
The 66 listing-linked venues currently have no path, SEO, layout, preview, or frontend detail renderer.
The virtual /venue/ archive has an approved collection route owner but no target frontend route or index configuration.
The virtual /market-coverage/ archive has an approved collection route owner but no target frontend route or index configuration.

validationGates.assertion: The versioned content-architecture document parses against its Zod contract.

Every currently implemented top-level and nested Payload block slug has one renderer branch, and importer-emitted block types belong to the implemented library. Planned production blocks are validated separately.
Every observed page, article, component, taxonomy, and supported shortcode semantic has a target disposition. Implemented importer coverage and planned target coverage are distinguished explicitly.

A reproducible production inventory proves the approved 296 public routes: 51 page documents, two virtual indexes, 90 posts, 66 venues, 72 hubs, and 15 learning videos, with FAQ included and Commodities Report excluded.
One canonical public path can be owned by at most one route owner across pages, articles, hubs, venues, learning videos, virtual indexes, and redirects.
validationGates.remediation: Add a shared route registry or cross-collection validation and reject conflicting create, update, publish, redirect, and migration operations. Remove reliance on pages-before-articles-before-hubs resolver precedence.

validationGates.assertion: Page, article, hub, venue, learning-video, and virtual-index archetypes enforce route policy, required fields, and allowed blocks or derived-route behavior.
validationGates.remediation: Add the approved page types, venue modes, learning-video owner, virtual-index configuration, conditional field requirements, and publication hooks; mirror constraints in the admin UI and importer.

validationGates.assertion: Every published internal article listing destination owns a complete Payload body; metadata-only records are non-routable or have an explicit external destination or redirect.
validationGates.remediation: Extract and transform every in-scope article body, or add an explicit destination model and prevent listing-only records from owning internal published paths.

validationGates.assertion: Every listing-linked article, hub, venue, and learning video resolves to one complete managed public route owner, while dependency-only records remain non-routable.
validationGates.remediation: Migrate complete bodies and route metadata for 90 posts, 72 hubs, 66 venues, and 15 learning videos; implement the learning-videos owner and venue detail renderer; validate every listing destination against the shared route registry.

validationGates.assertion: Structural column handling and the form, checklist, lifecycle, market-matrix, office, markets-map, regions, and cookie-preferences targets have Payload schemas, importer mappings, renderers, and behavior tests.
validationGates.remediation: Implement each planned catalogue entry end to end. Form handling must be first-party and support both page and article source layouts; [wcc_category_list] must become explicit consent-category behavior rather than generic shortcode execution.

validationGates.assertion: Internal links in navigation, actions, feature lists, entity lists, and rich text are managed references or are validated against the shared route namespace; path changes create or require redirects.
validationGates.remediation: Reuse a managed link field for CTA-bearing blocks, preserve internal source references during transformation, validate rich-text links, and integrate redirect creation with route changes.

validationGates.assertion: Every editor-visible control changes validated frontend behavior or is removed from the schema.
validationGates.remediation: Make marketCoverage.regions constrain the hub query, make dataChart.dataType select the correct dataset and rendering, implement embed.poster behavior, and add field-level behavior tests.

validationGates.assertion: Editors can author and publish in-scope content but cannot delete content, manage users or roles, or mutate migration provenance; administrators retain destructive and account controls.
validationGates.remediation: Extend access tests across globals, redirects, media, taxonomies, publish operations, versions, and direct API attempts to mutate provenance.

validationGates.assertion: The load resolves every legacy relationship token or fails with an explicit unresolved-reference report.
Re-running a migration upserts by stable source identity and content hash without duplicating records.
Payload stores editorial chart configuration only; imported market facts are loaded transactionally into app.market_volume_monthly.
Missing media, fallback alt text, stale links, legacy host rewrites, SEO normalization, and curated exclusions have explicit decisions before launch.
validationGates.remediation: Turn launch-critical review categories into configurable failure thresholds and record reviewer disposition alongside each item.
